basis: The Science description establishes an exceptionally tall crest; public coverage reports about 50 cm. The exact living height remains reconstruction-sensitive.
The describing paper states that an isometrically scaled bony crest would measure about 40 cm in length. The lower bound allows for reconstruction uncertainty.
No published transverse crest thickness was found in the accessible description. This deliberately broad range must be replaced with CT or scaled specimen measurements.
UCPC-2 is 62 mm high at its apex, but the crest is eroded and its original height is unknown. The upper bound prevents treating the preserved fragment as a complete crest.
UCPC-2 is 180 mm long. The interval treats that incomplete element as a conservative geometric baseline rather than a whole-skull reconstruction.
UCPC-2 is 52 mm wide at its widest point. The lower bound allows for a tapered crest section.
The published S. aegyptiacus flesh model estimated slow swimming at less than 1 m/s. This model samples only that stated range.
A head-first water entry or lunge can be faster than sustained swimming. This deliberately broad range is a scenario input, not a reconstructed Spinosaurus speed.
Fraction of crest height underwater during a crest-contact episode. The model intentionally does not assign drag when the crest remains dry during wading.
Angle between crest plane and local flow during an off-axis head movement. This exposes the lateral crest profile progressively from 15 to 90 degrees.
Broad sensitivity range for pressure drag on an incompletely reconstructed edge-on biological structure. It is not a CFD-derived value.

The reconstruction shows a crest that rises near-perpendicular to the snout, so the head-first-entry case uses a higher leading-edge pressure coefficient than steady aligned swimming. It is not a CFD-derived value.
Sensitivity range spanning a bluff, plate-like lateral profile. It is not a CFD-derived value.
Sensitivity range for turbulent skin friction on uncertain rough biological surfaces. It is not a CFD-derived value.
Freshwater reference density used for a riverine sensitivity analysis.
